claims.claim: Gen Digital links consumer digital dependence to cyber safety, identity protection and now financial-wellness tooling; the structural thesis is a shared consumer trust/distribution layer rather than a single-product security bottleneck.
MoneyLion can broaden cross-sell and engagement, but the causal bridge only strengthens if combined distribution improves retention or monetization without diluting security-brand trust.

falsifiers: cross-sell fails to improve retention or monetization
financial-wellness expansion weakens focus without durable cohort economics

claims.claim: Raised guidance and >$5B FY26 revenue support current execution, but acquisition-assisted consolidated growth cannot by itself establish organic product health.
The key present risk is integration and attribution: MoneyLion can make headline growth look stronger while product-level retention and synergy realization remain unproven.

risks.risk: Acquisition effects can obscure organic retention and monetization trends.
Expansion beyond cyber safety creates integration and strategic-focus risk.

unknowns.unknown: Product-level cohort retention, organic contribution and long-run MoneyLion unit economics are not established by current evidence.

falsifiers: organic retention deteriorates while consolidated growth remains acquisition-led
cross-sell synergies fail to appear after integration
